summary.text: The Kuiper belt is a disc of small bodies in the outer Solar System, stretching from Neptune's orbit at 30 AU to about 50 AU from the Sun.
It is similar to the asteroid belt but far larger, and most of its objects are made largely of frozen volatiles such as methane, ammonia and water.
It is home to most of the objects that astronomers generally accept as dwarf planets, including Pluto.

facts.label: Named for
facts.value: Dutch astronomer Gerard Kuiper, who conjectured it in 1951

facts.label: 1992 discovery
facts.value: 15760 Albion, the first one found since Pluto and Charon

facts.label: Big objects
facts.value: More than 100,000 over 100 km across are thought to exist

facts.label: Versus asteroid belt
facts.value: 20 times as wide and 20 to 200 times as massive

facts.label: Largest member
facts.value: Pluto, the largest and most massive known member

items.prompt: Studies since the mid-1990s show the Kuiper belt is dynamically stable. Where do comets with orbits under 200 years actually come from?

options.label: The Oort cloud, which is far more distant
The scattered disc, created by Neptune's outward motion
The asteroid belt between Mars and Jupiter
The rings and moons of the giant planets

items.explain: The true place of origin is the scattered disc, a dynamically active zone created by the outward motion of Neptune 4.5 billion years ago.

items.prompt: A spacecraft samples a typical Kuiper belt object and a typical asteroid. How do they likely differ?

options.label: The Kuiper object is rock and metal; the asteroid is ices
Both are made almost entirely of solid iron and nickel
Both are made largely of frozen methane and water
The Kuiper object is mostly ices; the asteroid rock and metal

items.explain: Many asteroids are mostly rock and metal, while most Kuiper belt objects are largely frozen volatiles such as methane, ammonia and water.

items.prompt: Pluto is the largest known Kuiper belt member. How did that membership affect its status in 2006?

options.label: It led to Pluto being reclassified as a dwarf planet
It confirmed Pluto as the ninth planet for good
It turned Pluto into a moon of Neptune
It had no effect, and Pluto stayed a full planet

items.explain: Pluto's status as part of the Kuiper belt caused it to be reclassified as a dwarf planet in 2006.

items.prompt: Plutinos are Kuiper belt objects whose orbits resemble Pluto's. What do they share?

options.label: A similar size and mass to Pluto itself
An orbit that crosses the path of Jupiter
The same 2:3 orbital resonance with Neptune
A large companion moon, as Pluto itself has

items.explain: Plutinos share the same 2:3 resonance with Neptune that characterizes Pluto's orbital period.

items.prompt: Gerard Kuiper wrote about a disc of leftover bodies in 1951, yet it is still unclear who deserves credit for the idea. Why?

options.label: He never published the idea, so only rumors survive
Many people floated similar ideas before and after him
Telescopes had already spotted the belt before he wrote
He later took back the claim that the disc existed

items.explain: The number and variety of earlier and later speculations leave continued uncertainty about who first proposed it.

items.prompt: Centaurs have orbits that last only a few million years. What did astronomers conclude from that?

options.label: They must be pieces broken off Jupiter's moons
They must form from dust near the Sun each time
They must be topped up from an outer reservoir
They must be rare, one-off visitors from other stars

items.explain: Because centaurs' orbits are unstable, astronomers speculated they must be frequently replenished by some outer reservoir.
